title: On iPhone the permission questions talk about the hidden AI coach, not what the app really uses
what: When the iPhone app asks for the camera, photos or microphone, the reason it shows was written for the AI coach: snap a meal for nutrition, talk to your AI coach, log meals by voice. The coach is switched off. The real uses are scanning the gym poster, progress and profile photos, and speaking a feedback message. The poster scanner has no reason line of its own, and two parts of the app give two different microphone reasons, so which one shows is down to build order. Apple turns apps away when the reason does not match what the app does with the permission.
expected: Before the iPhone app is sent to Apple, each permission reason says what the app really does today: scan your gym's poster, add progress and profile photos, speak a feedback message.
who: members on iPhone, and MettleUp at App Store review
how_often: once the iPhone app is sent for review
fix_line: Rewrite the camera, photos, microphone and speech reasons to match today's uses and give the poster scanner its own camera reason

title: The Credits page leaves out the app's icon set and the free code it is built on
what: The Credits page lists the exercise pictures, the body map and the fonts, but nothing else. The app's icons are drawn in the style of the free Lucide icon set, and at least one (the flame) is Lucide's drawing exactly. The app is also built from many free code packages whose licences ask that their short copyright notice comes with every copy. Neither the icon set nor the code packages are named anywhere in the app.
expected: The Credits page (or a 'free software used' page linked from it) names the icon set and lists the code packages with their licence notices.
fix_line: Add the icon set to the Credits list and a generated list of free code packages with their notices
